Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Manage acute asthma flare with escalation of bronchodilator therapy, introduction of monitoring tools, and close follow-up.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Wheeze with shortness of breath for about 2–3 days; productive status unclear; cough present; fever reported.
- Onset, duration, progression: Acute symptoms began ~2–3 days ago; fever noted (temperature around 37°C).
- History of presenting illness: Prior asthma (childhood; had an inhaler; stopped ~3–4 years ago). Adult history unclear for current control. Hay fever and eczema also reported.
- Past medical history: Asthma (childhood; past use of inhaler; not consistently used in past few years), hay fever, eczema.
- Medications: Salbutamol inhaler used in the past; current dosing not documented. No other medications reported.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Social history: Non-smoker. Drinks about one glass of wine every 2–3 days. Lives with partner. Occupation: engineer; has been working from home or on sick leave recently due to symptoms.
- Other: No peak flow meter at home; no spacer at home. Previously used inhalers; patient can use inhaler but spacer use is not established.

Objective:
- Vitals/Physical exam: Not documented in transcript except self-reported fever (~37°C). No other objective findings recorded.
- Symptoms reported by patient: Wheeze and shortness of breath on exertion; unable to exercise; able to climb stairs; can have difficulty completing sentences at times.
- Examinations or tests performed: None described.
- Past treatments documented: Salbutamol inhaler used previously; regularly used inhaled therapy in the past; current inhaler regimen not documented.
- Allergies: None reported.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute asthma exacerbation
- Assessment: Acute asthma flare likely given history of wheeze, shortness of breath with exertion, and prior asthma; possible triggers include pollen or viral infection (per patient history and clinician impression).
- Differential diagnoses: Viral respiratory infection with bronchospasm; other causes of dyspnea/exertional limitation not documented.
- Investigations planned: Peak flow monitoring to quantify airflow (to be prescribed); baseline monitoring at home (morning and evening).
- Treatment planned:
  - Increase inhaled short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) use to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
  - Provide spacer to improve inhaler delivery; pharmacist to instruct on use (spacer at home not currently available).
  - Consider a follow-up asthma review in about 1 week to assess control and possible initiation of additional controller therapy.
  - If fever worsens or wheeze worsens, contact clinic immediately.
- Referrals: None at this time; plan for a formal review in about one week; potential escalation to additional controller therapy if needed after review.

2. Asthma self-management optimization
- Assessment: History of past inhaler use; currently no spacer or peak flow meter; improvement needed in self-management.
- Differential diagnoses: Not applicable.
- Investigations planned: Peak flow meter to be prescribed; home monitoring to be reviewed.
- Treatment planned:
  - Provide peak flow meter (to be prescribed) and spacer (not currently owned); pharmacist to teach use.
  - Educate on recording peak flow values: first thing in the morning and in the evening for the next week; discuss results by phone.
- Referrals: Not required at this time; plan for follow-up discussion after monitoring data.

3. Allergic rhinitis (hay fever) management
- Assessment: History of hay fever; currently not taking regular antihistamines.
- Differential diagnoses: Allergic rhinitis symptoms overlapping with respiratory symptoms.
- Investigations planned: none.
- Treatment planned:
  - Initiate regular antihistamine (to be obtained from pharmacy).
- Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No documented vitals beyond self-reported temperature; no oxygen saturation or blood pressure; no physical exam findings; no documented peak expiratory flow value or spirometry; no exact inhaler names/doses/routines beyond “salbutamol” use; no documented medication allergies beyond “no allergies.”
- Internal conflicts: Patient occasionally unable to recall exact ages or years of past asthma management and specific inhaler types; no definite conflicts in the clinical content, but gaps exist in history details.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; few moments of recall uncertainty by patient (noted above) but content coherent.

Notes:
- All statements are based solely on the provided transcript. No external data or assumptions were added.
